edgeSemanticsPolicy: Every authored or derived vertex is WGS84 longitude/latitude. Consecutive vertices are joined by straight segments in longitude/latitude (plate carree). Before tiling, every segment is densified so that Mercator, great-circle and rhumb interpretations agree to within densifyToleranceMetres.

features.name: Suez Canal
features.gameplayReason: Route r_suez_canal links the Ottoman Egypt coast to the Red Sea in the 1880 content; it is the only sea shortcut between Mediterranean and Indian Ocean lanes, so a sealed isthmus would misrepresent the campaign map.

provenance.notes: Centreline only; width is a deliberate cartographic exaggeration to renderedWidthPixels.

features.validationNotes: Natural Earth 10m land seals the isthmus along this centreline; the overlay line is the only water representation.

features.name: Panama Canal
features.gameplayReason: Connects Caribbean and Pacific lane groups for post-1914 scenarios; display-only in the 1880 campaign, kept so the map does not show a sealed isthmus once the era gate opens.

provenance.notes: Centreline includes the lake section; locks are not represented.

features.validationNotes: Not an 1880 feature: opensYear gates it to later eras and the renderer must not show it before then.

features.name: Corinth Canal
features.gameplayReason: Cuts the Peloponnese isthmus between the Gulf of Corinth and the Aegean for post-1893 eastern Mediterranean coastal movement; display-only.

provenance.source: Bluewave-authored polyline from general public geographic knowledge of the published endpoints and course; not traced from any map image or proprietary dataset
provenance.notes: Two-point centreline from the published end locations (Poseidonia and Isthmia). Length checked at about 6.3 km, consistent with the published canal length. Accuracy is schematic until replaced by an approved dataset (ticket G-04a).

features.validationNotes: Width is below one pixel at every supported level; the overlay is a deliberate exaggeration.

features.name: Kiel Canal
features.gameplayReason: Port 'ger_kiel' (level 8) and route r_north_baltic tie the German North Sea and Baltic coasts together; the canal is the strategic internal link after 1895. Display-only.

provenance.source: Bluewave-authored polyline from general public geographic knowledge of the published endpoints and course; not traced from any map image or proprietary dataset
provenance.notes: Five-vertex schematic polyline between Brunsbuettel and Kiel-Holtenau through Rendsburg. It is a schematic course accurate to roughly 6 km, not a survey. Replace with an approved centreline (ticket G-04a).

features.validationNotes: Schematic: the validation checks representation and continuity, not survey accuracy.

provenance.source: Transect endpoints chosen on land either side of the passage from general geographic knowledge, then checked by script against the pinned Natural Earth land polygons; the passage itself is Natural Earth water
provenance.notes: referenceWidthMetres is the water width measured on the unsimplified pinned source along this transect, rounded; it is not a survey value

features.validationNotes: Natural Earth 10m keeps a water gap of about 1.1 km here; the strait is under one pixel wide below z5 and is guaranteed only from requiredFromZoom.

provenance.notes: Injected only when the pinned base land seals the passage along every transect. Replace with an approved centreline (ticket G-04a).
